newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin urges youth to study to be Russian leaders.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin urges youth to study to be Russian leaders.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin urged Russia's young people on Friday to study hard to create a team of young professionals who will rule the country in the 21st century.
"Russia has never had such a young elite. Recruitment to the team of leaders of the next century has just begun," Yeltsin said in a radio address.

The address was recorded on Thursday, before Yeltsin left for a meeting of the leaders of Group of Seven leading industrialised countries in the U.S. city of Denver. The summit is due to start on Friday.
In his address Yeltsin said Russia was developing rapidly, and its economy and politics needed young professionals.

"There is a construction and car boom in the country. Services and financial spheres are growing like a snowball. Your country now is one of the most promising in the world for young, energetic and intelligent people," he said.
Yeltsin pointed out that knowledge and not only business could bring some cash to those who prefer books to small trade.

"The real money is made with the head. A clever, intelligent head," he said, warning young Russians against leaving their studies for a handful of roubles they may make selling beverages in street kiosks.
